text: in stable COPD;1 it found small benefits on lung function outcomes and quality of life with ipratropium compared with a short-acting beta2 agonist; a reduction in the requirements for oral corticoster- oids was also seen. Combination therapy with ipratropium and a short-acting beta2 agonist was associated with some clinically meaningful lung function outcomes compared with the beta2 agonist alone, but these were not reflected in subjective improve- ments or symptom scores. A systematic review comparing ipratropium with a long-acting beta2 agonist in stable COPD,2 found that salmeterol had more effect than ipratropium on lung function, but no major differenc- es were seen between symptom responses to ipratropium and sal- meterol. Combination treatment with these two drugs was better than salmeterol alone in terms of quality of life. 1. Appleton S, et al. Ipratropium bromide is used intranasally for the treat- ment of rhinorrhoea in allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (p.565). It has also relieved rhinorrhoea and sneezing associated with the common cold. References. 1. Georgitis JW, et al.
